items.title: 仓库经理能一眼看清整个黑五仓库吗？Opus 5.5 做的 93 人、320 台机器人实时 3D 仿真
items.description: Konstantin Saifoulline（@konstantinsaifo，Airsup）2026-10-19 帖串：大多数仓库经理从没一次看到整个作业现场，于是让 Claude Opus 5.5 做了俯视视角——黑五当天 93 人、320 台机器人和所有卡车实时运行（主帖约 1000 赞）。本条回复给出在线版 https://www.airsup.ai/lab/warehouse-ops ：点任何人看他去哪；每个人走真实路线（通道、跨越处、休息室），所有机器人、叉车、卡车跑在同一个全天离散事件仿真里；一个发现：离休息室最远的拣货员约四分之一休息时间花在来回路上。视频画面可见：俯视 3D 仓库（入库区、收货台、QA 测试区、码头），右侧面板为吞吐量对计划、在途订单、机器人/叉车利用率、人员分布、QA、存储，底部为码头排班，告警栏显示「卡车 IN-129 迟到→门已重排」。网页加载 three.js 模块（GTAO、RoundedBoxGeometry 等）。作者公开过的通用做法（均有出处）：①开源 Claude Code skill「factory-skill」（https://github.com/AirsupHQ/factory-skill ，作者帖 https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2109974620698775744 ：用 Claude Opus 5.5 做的开源 skill，一句话描述工厂即生成带离散事件仿真的 3D 工厂；README：npx skills add AirsupHQ/factory-skill -g -a claude-code，然后 /factory <一句话>，输出单个自包含 HTML、零依赖）；②开源 airsup-lab（https://github.com/AirsupHQ/airsup-lab ，MIT）README：纯 TypeScript + three.js、无框架、无模型文件，所有部件加载时由代码程序化生成；剖切、流线、物理先行、确定性 step(dt)；tools/record.mjs 用 Playwright 逐帧步进+ffmpeg 录 60fps 成片，每台机器有脚本化镜头巡游；③作者经验帖 https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2110682133589062119 ：同时跑一小队 Claude agent 日夜搭仿真，要点是核对 agent 实际用的模型、笔记本最多同时跑 2 个重型构建、别给 agent 截止时间、一个 brief 只做一件事、人是质量关。 本作品的具体提示词未公开；作者在帖串称这是「the V3 Black Friday warehouse」，另有第二个仓库版本。

items.title: 书柜为什么拧半圈就能锁紧？把宜家 BILLY 的真实说明书一页页搬进 3D：82 个五金件按图纸顺序逐个装上，还能切到说明书线稿视角（Three.js）
items.description: Ryan Sael 的网页作品「Flat Pack, Step by Step」：左边是宜家 BILLY 书柜原版装配说明书（AA-1823127-9，16 页，原样展示并链回原件），右边 3D 场景按说明书一步步装——14 步、11 块板、82 个五金件（16 个木销、12 个偏心螺钉、12 个偏心锁件、18 根钉子、16 个层板托、2 个墙固定件等），「已装入」计数实时跟着走，每步的视角大致对齐图纸角度；可切「房间 / 线稿」两种视图、爆炸图、点击零件读出名称编号，另有 LACK 边桌（4 根双头螺丝 + 4 条腿）。页面自带原理讲解：偏心锁件——偏心螺钉先拧进侧板，装上横板时螺钉头落进板面的圆形凸轮里，顺时针转半圈，螺钉头沿凸轮内的螺旋坡被拉紧；木销只负责对位，背板钉上后才防止柜体歪斜。作者也写明哪些是精确的（零件、数量、顺序、五金编号来自说明书），哪些是读图估计的（板厚、孔位、层板高度）。X 帖 10-19 发布，约 4100 赞。可作科普镜头：偏心锁件的螺旋坡原理、爆炸图到装配的结构叙事、「说明书为什么要两个人抬」；也可借鉴给创作者的「房间 3D 化」想法。

items.title: 瓶子里的水晃得像真的，为什么一行流体模拟都没跑？《Barely Breathing》用速度驱动着色器「假晃动」+ 局部/世界双坐标水线
items.description: Jettelly 采访独立游戏《Barely Breathing》开发者 Jaspreet Singh Matharoo：容器里的水不是流体模拟，而是着色器效果——一个高度参数决定水有多满，脚本读取容器速度、驱动着色器里的两个旋转让液面晃动（晃动脚本致谢 MinionsArt）。只用容器局部坐标，水面会跟着瓶子僵硬倾斜；只用世界坐标，液面保持水平，但瓶子上移时水线会掉在后面——他把两者混合：水线跟着容器走、液面仍能晃；再在第一道高度切线略下方加第二道切线，做出一圈随水线移动的泡沫带。水体外壳用 Blender Solidify 加薄层并翻转法线、单独材质；自定义深度渐隐按身后物体距离改透明度与颜色；顶点色分别标出「去掉泡沫的顶面」和「该起泡的边缘」，再用动画噪声打破轮廓；同一着色器换参数就能做茶、咖啡、阴沟水。可作科普镜头：惯性让液面滞后的直觉、局部 vs 世界坐标系、「看起来像物理」与「真算物理」的成本差。
items.tool: Unity 着色器 + C# 速度脚本（晃动脚本源自 MinionsArt）+ Blender Solidify

items.title: 纸纹着色器为什么只能当背景？鼠标划过，整页网页像纸一样起皱再慢慢抚平——Codrops「PaperDrops」把 Paper 着色器搬到 DOM 元素上（WebGPU / domgl）
items.description: Jesper Landberg 在 Codrops 的过程文：先用设计工具 Paper 画一个虚构工作室站 PaperDrops，再把 Paper 着色器库里的 GLSL 着色器手工移植成 WGSL，跑在他自己的 WebGPU 库 domgl 上——domgl 把普通 DOM 元素镜像成同一张 GPU 画布上的平面，文字和图片仍留在页面里负责布局、无障碍与文本选中。纸纹不再是全屏背景，而是整帧渲染后的后处理：只在光标附近起皱、离开后慢慢抚平，文字和图片一起弯；项目卡片用跟随光标、带阻尼的透镜畸变；分区用 warp 着色器画撕纸边。打光时发现折痕部分输出的其实是位置而不是折叠——每格一道慢坡，静图看不出，一打光就露出大块明暗与硬对角线，滤掉慢坡只留细节才解决。还用 Paper 的 MCP 让 Claude Code 直接读写设计稿（含 55 个 token），先写移动端代码再回写成 Paper 画板。可作科普镜头：纸褶的法线与打光、为什么「静态看着对、一打光就穿帮」。
items.tool: Paper（设计工具 + 着色器库 + MCP）、domgl（WebGPU / WGSL）、Claude Code、Tailwind v4

items.title: 纸不会变长：用弧长守恒做卷、折、垂、揉，再用摄像头辨火焰、对着吹就能烧穿——开源 paperlab（React + Three.js）
items.description: Codrops 2026-10-18 案例：设计师/工程师 Noor Mtir（Nawwara Studio）开源 React 库 paperlab，把纸当成真实几何而不是两张假折的平面。核心规则：弧长守恒——绕半径 r 的圆柱卷曲时，距起点 s 的点转过 s/r，纸既不拉长也不缩短；对比用正弦位移「弯」纸，字会抹开、一眼假。库提供 roll/curl/bend/fold 与 wave/drape/crumple 等变形器，另有 peel、letter-fold、unroll 等行为预设；同一套数学有 CPU（可交互抓角）与 GPU 实例化（几十张纸一趟画）双实现，用黄金向量门禁防漂移。后半部分把手势砍到「只烧纸」：MediaPipe 读手与嘴型，用颜色+闪烁算术识别真实打火机火焰（不靠火焰模型），再叠 CPU 损伤网格（炭/水/热/剩余纸，沿纤维导热更快所以洞呈椭圆）、GPU 稳定流体火焰、灰烬粒子与发光。损伤网格也驱动布料：烧断的那块会掉下去。npm 包 paperlab，文档与编辑器见 paperlab.nawwara.studio，源码 github.com/NourMtir0722/Paperlab。科普镜头：①为什么「看起来像折」其实在拉伸；②火焰是燃料遇见空气的界面，不是一团热烟上色；③和用户已赞的揉皱纸/布料物理同一路。

items.description: X 用户 @geek_zard 10 月 18 日发布约 15 秒竖屏对照视频，上下分屏：一半是用 three.js 代码搭的低模白模画面，一半是可灵 Kling 4.0 视频编辑重绘后的写实画面。第一段是城市高架路，一辆车整个翻成底朝天，从公交车和货车上方飞越车流；第二段在隧道口，车先出现在隧道口上沿倒挂的位置，随后落到车流前方，周围是出租车和私家车。作者说这类「车贴墙、倒挂、翻转、飞越车流」的反直觉动作，纯提示词和首尾帧都控制不住，最后靠 3D 白模 + 可灵视频编辑跑通，并列出要点：白模用 three.js 写代码搭、逐帧渲染，相机对齐上一段的尾帧，衔接才无缝；车的侧倾角按隧道截面的弧度计算，四个轮子才能始终贴墙；白模车别用方盒子，要接近真车轮廓的流线型，否则倒挂时可灵只能靠猜、车会变形；白模车和场景用同色调的泥塑灰，把光线也做进白模，可灵才会重新上色而不是照搬 CG 质感；可灵设置的生成时长要和白模视频一致，多出来的部分没有白模约束，模型会自己编；和白模布局冲突的参考图一律去掉。科普/制作用途：①直接演示「视频模型只会补画面、不懂物理，要靠 3D 骨架约束」；②正好是「房间 3D 建模→换装修风格」项目可借的做法：同一个白模房间，换提示词重绘成不同风格，结构不会跑。

items.description: X 用户 @my189 10 月 18 日发布约 13 秒 4K 横屏录屏，称 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 一次写通「磁吸倒挂 + RCS 冷气翻滚 + 反推缓降 + 悬挂回弹」整套连续物理状态。画面是夜间测试场，探照灯和镜头眩光很强，四周是 HUD 式数据面板，左下角依次打出阶段名：APPROACH（接近）、C-LOOP ASCENT（爬上 C 形弧道）、INVERTED HOLD（倒挂静止）、POWERED DESCENT（动力下降）、SOFT TOUCHDOWN（软着陆）、TEST COMPLETE / TOUCHDOWN CONFIRMED。作者公开了完整提示词：描述一辆白色跑车冲上巨大的金属 C 形弧形坡道，在顶部 180 度倒置处靠车底吸附风扇倒挂静止，1 秒后脱离轨道，车底反推喷口持续喷白色冷气减速，车身四周再爆发几道冷气脉冲（无明火）完成 180° 横滚回正，接近地面时向下喷白雾缓冲，四轮柔和接地、避震压缩回弹，手持长焦跟拍，要求用 Three.js + SVG 构建。作者建议换载具或受力状态就能改成自己的交互主页。科普用途：可借这套「分阶段受力状态」写法做反推、喷气姿态控制、悬挂回弹的示意镜头。

items.title: 把磁铁推近线圈，电压表就跳一下：Induction Bench 用 Three.js 把磁感线、法拉第定律和楞次定律做成能拖能调的桌面实验（Opus 5.5）
items.description: X 用户 The Bugged Dev（@thebuggeddev，库内已收其毛绒蜘蛛作品）9 月 28 日发布约 71 秒录屏，称这是用 Claude Opus 5.5 做的电磁场可视化，原帖约 2,800 赞、1,600 收藏；10 月 18 日又被 @Jomolos 转介绍为「Induction Bench」。画面是一张网页实验台：中间黑底 3D 视图里一块磁铁和一个铜线圈，磁铁周围画满弯曲的磁感线；右上角是检流计表盘，指针随磁铁移动左右摆；下方两张小图分别是示波器式的电压曲线和「磁通量/电压随磁铁位置变化」曲线；左侧面板可以切换磁铁种类（N42、N52、钐钴 SmCo 等）、线圈导线材料（铜、银、铝、镍铬）、匝数和铁芯。录屏里磁铁从远处靠近、穿过线圈、再离开，电压先正后负；也演示了换成电磁铁、加铁芯后磁感线变密。按 @Jomolos 的说明：线圈里的磁通量随时间变化才会产生电压，磁铁不动就没有，反向移动电压反向（法拉第定律）；感应电流总是阻碍引起它的变化（楞次定律）；代码里为不同材料设了不同物理参数，铁芯等复杂部件用的是近似模型，不是实验室测量值。科普镜头：发电机、无线充电、电磁炉都是这一个原理，可直接截这张实验台当「为什么磁铁动起来才有电」的第一帧。

items.title: 一句提示词让 DeepSeek 做出整台电脑主机：按真实装机顺序一步步装上主板、水冷、显卡、玻璃侧板，再一步步拆回空机箱
items.description: LemoLab 作者 Lemomo（@lemomo_ai）10月18日发布约 57 秒横屏录屏，自称用 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 一次生成（one shot），是「穷玩车、富玩表、屌丝玩电脑」系列继机械表拆解之后的电脑篇。公开的提示词是：写一个单文件 HTML，做一台尽可能多组件、材质真实的台式电脑主机，按真实装机顺序动画演示组装和拆解过程，支持一键播放。画面是深蓝灰背景下的一台中塔机箱，左侧是步骤列表和说明文字，底部是播放进度条；本轮截帧看到的步骤包括「主板入箱」「安装一体水冷」「安装玻璃侧板」「理顺线材」，之后反向「拆除一体水冷」「拆除主板」，最后剩一个空机箱和标着 NOVA 的电源；装好后能看到三把带灯圈的风扇、显卡和冷排。作者随后又发了同一提示词下 DeepSeek 与 GPT-6 Astra 的对比，并说明单次生成不能证明哪个模型更好。科普镜头：「一台电脑由哪些零件组成、按什么顺序装」可直接拿来当爆炸图/装配动画；同一套「步骤列表 + 一键播放的装配时间轴」也能套到光刻机、晶圆盒、封装结构的拆解上。

items.title: 一套程序化的微缩世界地块：雪山垭口、樱花瀑布、沙漠水塔，都在浏览器里用 WebGI 实时渲染、可以进去逛

items.title: Colorfigures：手绘等距线稿的日常物件，点一点就能看懂洗衣机、咖啡机怎么工作
items.description: April（@Aprilzz423）2026-10-17 发帖：她也在探索「边玩边学」，做了一个 Claude skill，用来生成手绘风格、可交互的日常物件，帖内约 49 秒视频演示她的小洗衣机。帖子引用 @wheresryan22 的儿童版原型「打气筒是怎么给轮胎充气的？」（他在试不同版本，想找到既简单又足够有细节、能让孩子互动学习的方式）。帖中链接的作品站 Colorfigures 自述「Hand-inked isometric figures you can play with」，目前收录 17 个物件：洗衣机、意式咖啡机、自动售货机、烤面包机、微波炉、削笔刀、发条玩具、红绿灯、烟雾报警器、冰箱、音乐盒、马桶冲水、扭蛋机、拍照亭、街机、餐车、厕所隔间，←→ 切换。可拍角度：①「东西是怎么工作的」做成可点的手绘图；②给孩子的交互科普；③一个 skill 批量出同风格物件。

items.title: 站在车站能看见多远的山？一个把地球曲率和大气折射都算进去的 360° 山景网页（Gemini 4 + Three.js）
items.description: 日本 X 用户 @sagami_ss_dev（さがみあーと）10月18日发布用 Gemini 4 Argon 做的网页应用「山並み360°｜淵野辺」，并附约 50 秒录屏。以 JR 淵野辺站（北纬 35.568°、东经 139.395°，海拔 121 米 + 眼高 1.6 米）为观察点，调用日本国土地理院的数据，把丹沢、秩父山系的山峰按真实三维坐标放进 360° 全景里，点击山名会显示海拔、简介和山上的小屋。本轮查看了网页源码：用 Three.js（r160）渲染，地球半径取 6,371,000 米，大气折射系数 k=0.13，每座山因地球弯曲「沉下去」的高度按 距离²÷(2×地球半径)×(1−k) 计算；山点列表里有大山（1252 米）、塔ノ岳（1491 米）、雲取山（2017 米，东京最高峰）、武甲山等几十个点。录屏画面朴素：浅蓝天空、绿色地形、山名标签沿地平线排开，右侧是信息面板。科普镜头：按页面里的公式，50 公里外的山会被地球曲率「藏掉」约 196 米，算上大气折射后约 171 米——这就是为什么远处的山看起来比实际矮、更远的高山会整个落到地平线以下；大气折射让光线略微向下弯，所以能看得比几何直线更远一点。可迁移成「在上海/深圳的高楼上能看多远」「为什么看得见海上的船先露出桅杆」这类镜头。

items.title: 能按、能捏、能扔的软萌玩具：同一句提示词，Opus 5.5 花 10 美元 51 分钟，GPT-6.1 花 1 美元 21 分钟（单文件 Three.js）
items.description: X 用户 Miles Sun（@realmilessun）10月18日发布约 43 秒竖屏对比视频：同一句提示词——做一个可以按压、拿起、捏扁、扔出去的「捏捏乐」软玩具，单个 HTML 文件、只用 three.js。上半屏是 Claude Opus 5.5（作者标注花费 10.04 美元、51 分钟），下半屏是 GPT-6.1-sol（1.03 美元、21 分钟）。两版都做成了标题为「Squishy.」的网页：吐司面包、牛油果、猫爪、蛋糕块、团子等软乎乎的小物件，鼠标按下去会凹陷回弹、可以拎起来扔，结尾两版都把一大堆玩具倒出来堆成小山；Opus 版的物件有柔和投影和更明显的回弹形变，右侧有计数面板。作者问「Opus 贵 10 倍，你会捏哪个？」，并写明「Made with Claude + ultramotion」。和库内已收藏的充气按钮、布料物理同属「可以上手捏的材质」。科普镜头：软体物理怎么让一块「面包」被按下去又弹回来（质点-弹簧/体积保持的直觉讲法）；同题不同模型的成本和耗时差 10 倍，可作为「AI 写代码到底花多少钱」的直观素材。

items.title: 没用一张生成图、一帧生成视频：Claude Code 用 Three.js 搭出会随年代变化的「动态历史地图」，从海底到武士之都的镰仓
items.description: 日本历史×AI 创作者くるみ（@kurumirekishi）10月18日发布约 1 分 57 秒竖屏视频《鎌倉——海の底から 武士の都へ》（从海底到武士之都）。作者说明：画面全部是代码，没有用图片生成或视频生成，是 Claude Code 用 Three.js 搭出地形模型、按时代让它动起来，配乐用 Suno，由 Opus 5.5 每天制作；她在 Instagram 上同系列的京都篇播放约 68 万次。视频像一张米黄纸底的立体地图：开头是「縄文のころ」海水退去露出三角形平地，随后依次出现 1063 年海边建起八幡宫、1192 年源赖朝任征夷大将军、1241 年左右「劈山开路」（切通）、1512 年玉绳城，一直到 1964–1966 年「市民守护山林」；每一段都有大号年份、标题字、地图上的标注点和移动的路线，海岸线和森林随年代变化。科普镜头：这套「同一块地形 + 时间轴驱动标注」的做法，可以直接套到「上海外滩 / 深圳湾 / 一座晶圆厂园区几十年的变化」这类选题；纸质地图风格也和库内纸艺类素材相近。

items.title: 整颗月球只是一个 72KB 的网页：站在 48 公里宽的陨石坑里，地平线只有 2.4 公里远，地球一动不动挂在天上（WebGPU，MIT）
items.description: X 用户 @tarasshyn（Taras Shynkarenko）10月17日发布：用 Claude Code + Opus 5.5 做的实时月面渲染器，打包后是一个约 72KB 的单 HTML 文件，WebGPU 直接跑、不用游戏引擎，在线可玩（tarasshynkarenko.com/moon，需新版 Chrome），源码开源（GitHub TarasShyn/moon-surface，MIT）。作者注明它基于库内已收的 web-ocean（Maksymilian Dendura / GitHub Noniv）的架构，bloom 和 AgX 色调映射代码按 MIT 许可改编。画面：开局站在一个 48 公里的复杂陨石坑里，地球挂在坑沿上方；陨石坑小到厘米级，还有石块、柔和阴影、弯曲的地平线和缓慢转动的星空；按 G 进入月球重力行走（空格跳），Z 键 6° 望远看地球，H 键调太阳、地照、曝光、星空延时等。README 写明的物理细节正好是科普素材：①月球半径 1737.4 公里，地面按 d²/2R 下沉，从人眼高度看地平线只有约 2.4 公里远，30 公里外的坑壁会「沉」下去几百米；②月壤用 McEwen（1991）的月球-朗伯反射模型加「冲日效应」，所以没有临边昏暗、顺着太阳方向看去地面又平又亮；③阴影是「0.53° 的太阳圆盘露出多少」算出来的软阴影；④阴影里的补光来自被照亮地面的反射和地照，地照强度随地球的相位变化——把太阳降到地平线下、曝光加到约 14 EV，就能看到只被地球照亮的月面；⑤星空和银河以朔望月周期（29.5 天一圈）乘 4000 倍延时绕月极转动，地球自转、云层飘动，但地球在天上的位置不动，「就像从月球正面看到的那样」。地形由 6 层 1024×1024 的 GPU 程序化纹理叠成（周期从 131 公里到 3.3 米），陨石坑的深度、坑缘、平底、阶地和中央峰都按半径和年龄生成，年轻的坑带亮色溅射物和辐射纹。科普镜头：为什么月球上的地平线这么近；为什么满月看起来像一张平平的圆盘（没有临边昏暗）；为什么从月球上看，地球几乎不会升起落下（潮汐锁定）；什么是地照。

items.title: 你发出的一条消息，30 毫秒里走了 6000 公里：从咖啡桌上的手机、基站、登陆站到 4000 米深的海底光缆，钻进 9 微米的玻璃纤芯（@techartist_）
items.description: X 用户 @techartist_（库内已收其水磨坊、泡澡球作品）10月17日发布约 29 秒的 3D 短片《一条消息从咖啡桌到海外数据中心的旅程》。画面是带时间轴和播放控件的网页式 3D 场景，每一站左上角都有标签显示累计距离、信号时间和深度（均标注「约」「已放慢」）：The Phone（约 0.1 km）——「你的消息以无线电波离开手机」；The Tower（约 1 km，0.006 ms）——「基站把它送进光纤，变成光」；The Coast（约 25 km）——「在登陆站进入跨洋海缆」；The Seabed（约 447 km，2.23 ms，水深约 4000 m）——「洲际互联网流量大多走海底」，画面里有 ROV 的探照灯和中继器；The Cable（约 2058 km，10.3 ms）——「里面是头发丝细的玻璃纤维」；Inside the Fibre（约 3350 km 处，16.8 ms）——标注纤芯约 9 µm、包层约 125 µm、1550 nm 红外光脉冲（假色可视化），字幕「光被全反射困在玻璃纤芯里」「多种颜色共用一根光纤，各自携带数据」；The Data Centre（约 6065 km，30.3 ms）——「几十毫秒就跨过了一片海」。作者同晚另发一条姊妹片（https://x.com/techartist_/status/2111615745234751794），用 3D 拟物演示「点发送之后」的 TLS 握手到解密：明文谁都能读、AES-GCM/ChaCha20 加密后「同一条消息换了伪装」、路由器逐跳转发时只看得到去向和大小、看不到内容。科普镜头：用片中自己的数字就能算出光在光纤里的速度（6065 km ÷ 30.3 ms ≈ 每秒 20 万公里，约为真空光速的 2/3，因为玻璃折射率约 1.5）；全反射如何把光困在纤芯里；波分复用「多种颜色共用一根光纤」；为什么跨洋延迟有物理下限。也可迁移成「芯片里的信号旅程」镜头语言。

items.title: 5000 只椋鸟和一只鹰：没人指挥，鸟群自己折叠、分裂又合拢（Three.js Boids，一句提示词）
items.description: X 用户 @TokenGremlin 10月17日发布约 28 秒录屏：作者称用 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017（开启 DeepThink）一句提示词生成的 Three.js 场景——夕阳下的湖面上空，5000 只椋鸟按 Boids 规则飞行，用空间哈希网格加速邻居查找；鸟群会自己折叠、分裂、再合拢，一只鹰俯冲进鸟群（也可以用鼠标操控鹰），湖面倒映整个鸟群。作者自评：太阳光晕过曝得厉害，但鸟群运动是真的像；在 2019 年的旧笔记本上跑得很卡。录屏里能看到鸟群从一团变成弧形「幕布」、再压扁成贴着水面的长带，鹰冲过的地方被撕开一个口子。科普镜头：这是「涌现」最直观的演示——每只鸟只遵守三条局部规则（别撞上邻居、和邻居同向、往群体中心靠），整体却出现谁也没设计过的形状；鹰的冲击让信息在群里一波波传开（真实椋鸟群也有这种躲避波）。可直接作为用户长期想做的「涌现」视频的开场备选，与库内 three.js GPGPU 鸟群选题互补（这条多了捕食者扰动）。

items.title: 一间「有人住过」的杂乱书房，全靠 AI 建模再自动搬进 UE5：Opus 把 Blender 材质逐个转成虚幻引擎着色器（@Yokohara_h）
items.description: 日本 3D 艺术家 Hirokazu Yokohara（@Yokohara_h，C4D/Maya/ZBrush/Blender/UE5）10月16日发布约 47 秒视频：「只用 AI 做的室内场景的实时版」——让 Opus 把场景从 Blender 自动移植到 UE5，作者说搬进游戏引擎本来非常麻烦，用 AI 方便得惊人，还打算用这个房间做个小恐怖游戏。画面是一间堆满书、纸箱、杂志和小物件的书房，午后阳光从百叶窗斜射进来，镜头缓慢游走。作者在回复中补充：场景结合了 AI 在 Blender 里直接建模和 AI 3D 生成工具，全部由 Opus 和 Astra 自动操控，「关键是把 AI 3D 生成整合进工作流」；全部是新做的资产；移植时让 Opus 把现成的 PBR 材质原样转换，对用 Blender 着色器节点做的材质只烘焙遮罩等必要元素、其余在 UE 里用虚幻着色器重建；画面质感来自 Lumen 和后处理；测试完会上传文件。帖子获约 1900 赞、15 万次浏览。对用户「房间 3D 建模 + 换装修风格」项目：这是「AI 建模 → 引擎实时渲染」的现成参考，尤其是材质迁移的做法——换风格本质上就是批量换材质和灯光。

items.title: 200 万段能直接运行的 3D 代码：让 AI 用 Blender Python / Three.js「写」出可修改的模型，同一个 Opus 5.5 换套流程，人评胜率从 21% 到 79%（Apache-2.0）
items.description: 南加州大学、耶鲁、罗切斯特、UCSD、哥大、南洋理工、UCSC、Google DeepMind 等作者的 3DCodeVerse（arXiv 2610.22341，2026-10-15 提交）：思路是「3D 世界就是代码」——所有资产都只用代码生成（Blender Python、Three.js、OpenGL 等），从单个物体、带关节的可动物体到整个场景和图形渲染。包含三部分：①3DCodeVerse-2M，约 200 万段可独立运行的 3D 程序，每段附源文件、素材、描述和验证记录（Hugging Face 数据集 ilabai/3dcodeverse）；②3DCodeVerse Harness，多智能体 DAG 流程：先规划 3D 项目，让各家编码代理写原始代码，再自动执行、测量空间尺寸、渲染并评判，根据反馈自动修改，生成过程中不需要人工反馈；③用该语料对 Qwen 做 LoRA/DPO 微调的开源基线。README 给出的 100 个文本生成 3D 物体测试：同一模型放进这套流程后都胜过自家原生工具——Claude Opus 5.5 从 Claude Code 换到 3DCodeVerse，人评偏好 21%→79%、评审分 77.2→88.5；对比 Claude Design（3D Object）为 10%→90%、37.4→87.7；Gemini 3.8 Flash 13%→87%；GPT-6 Astra（Codex）31%→69%。项目页 3dcodeverse.com 有布料、液体、破碎等物理场景和机械结构的展示视频。对用户的「房间 3D 建模 + 换装修风格」项目：代码生成的 3D 场景天然可参数化修改（换材质、换配色、改尺寸），比一次性生成的网格好改；科普角度可讲「为什么让 AI 写代码造 3D，比让它直接生成模型更容易验证和修改」。
items.tool: Blender Python / Three.js / OpenGL；编码代理含 Claude Opus 5.5、Gemini 3.8 Flash、GPT-6 Astra/Luna（README）；Qwen LoRA/DPO 微调

items.title: 摇得越久喷得越猛：一段公开的中文提示词做出可摇、可开盖、可倒的橘子汽水，Opus 5.5 和 Gemini 4 Argon 同题对比（$30 vs $2）
items.description: X 用户 @faustina5211314（一只橘）10月17日「橘子实验室 #2」：同一段提示词分别交给 Claude Opus 5.5 和 Gemini 4 Argon，各做一个单 HTML 文件（Three.js 从 CDN 引入，其余素材代码生成）。交互：按住瓶子左右拖动摇晃，液面晃荡、拍打瓶壁，摇得越久气泡越多；点瓶盖弹飞，泡沫从瓶口涌出、顺瓶身流下；往下拖倒进玻璃杯，杯里起泡浮沫；夕阳从窗外斜射，玻璃和汽水在桌面投出橙色焦散光斑；按 D 自动演示 17 秒录屏。作者对比：Argon 约半小时做完，泡沫像一串白球、倒出来一颗一颗往下滴；Opus 磨了约 2 小时，泡沫顺瓶身流到桌上堆着、倒出来是整条水柱、杯上浮一层泡沫，还有汽水蒸发和桌面水渍，成本约贵 15 倍。作者在评论区分 6 条贴出完整提示词（已收录）。科普镜头：为什么摇过的汽水一开盖就喷——溶解的二氧化碳需要「成核点」才能变成气泡，摇晃制造了大量微小气泡；也可作「同一提示词、不同模型」的成本/质量对比素材。
items.tool: Claude Opus 5.5 / Gemini 4 Argon + Three.js（单 HTML，作者自述）
items.prompt:
做一个「摇一摇再开盖的橘子汽水」，只用一个 HTML 文件完成（JS 和 CSS 写在里面，可以从 CDN 引入 Three.js，其他素材全部用代码生成），双击就能在浏览器里打开。

画面（写实风格）：
- 傍晚的木头桌面，桌上一瓶玻璃瓶装的橘子汽水，旁边半个切开的橘子和几颗水珠。
- 瓶子是透明玻璃，瓶身挂着凝结的水珠，金属瓶盖；瓶里是半透明的橙色汽水，液面上方留一截空气。
- 光线：窗外斜射进来的暖色夕阳是唯一的主光，玻璃和汽水把光折射到桌面上，形成橙色的焦散光斑。

交互：
1. 摇晃：按住瓶子左右拖动，瓶子跟着晃，液面真实地晃荡、拍打瓶壁，摇得越久气泡越多。
2. 开盖：点击瓶盖，瓶盖弹飞。摇得越久喷得越猛：泡沫从瓶口涌出、顺着瓶身流下，细小的气泡从瓶底一串串往上冒。这是最重要的画面。
3. 倒出来：按住瓶子往下拖，瓶子倾斜，汽水倒进旁边的玻璃杯，杯里起泡、浮起一层泡沫。
4. 视角：右键拖动旋转，滚轮缩放；左键只用来操作瓶子。
5. 「重来」按钮：换一瓶新的。

录屏用：
- 打开时的默认镜头要同时看到瓶子、瓶口上方的空间和桌面上的光斑。
- 按 D 进入演示模式，自动演一遍：0–3 秒镜头绕瓶子转半圈；3–7 秒用力摇晃；7–11 秒开盖喷涌，镜头停住；11–15 秒倒进杯子；15–17 秒杯里的气泡慢慢平静。
- 按 H 隐藏所有按钮和文字。

质量：
- 画面要像一张饮料广告照片，不要像早期 3D 游戏。
- 在集成显卡的笔记本上也要流畅；按 Q 在高、中两档画质之间切换。
- 做完后在浏览器里实际打开测一遍：控制台没有报错，开盖后能清楚看到泡沫喷出来，再交付。

items.title: 一滴水落进玻璃杯只用 127 毫秒：Three.js 把皇冠水花、瑞利-普拉托尖刺和沃辛顿射流按 1.7 万帧慢放给你看
items.description: X 用户 @josepcalull 10月17日发布约 15 秒竖版短片：一滴水落进玻璃杯的超慢镜头，作者称用 Claude Code 一句提示词生成、单个 HTML + Three.js、没用 3D 软件也没剪辑，并在自回复中贴出提示词。画面像高速摄影机回放：左上角 REC 与帧率读数（如 17,140 FPS、6,600 FPS、2,110 FPS）、右上角毫秒计时和「H₂O · 21 °C」，西班牙语字幕逐段解说——先是水滴撞击后溅起的「皇冠」（字幕：瑞利-普拉托不稳定性），再是空腔塌陷把水向上弹出的「沃辛顿射流」，最后「这一切发生在 127 毫秒内」。科普镜头：为什么水花会长成一圈尖刺（表面张力让液膜边缘断成一颗颗小液滴）、为什么水滴落下后反而有一柱水往上冲、高速摄影的帧率和慢放倍数怎么换算；可直接借这套「高速摄影 HUD + 分段字幕」的镜头语言做半导体工艺慢放（如液滴、溅射）。

items.description: X 用户 @theparuchh 10月17日发布约 50 秒对比视频：让 Claude Opus 5.5 和 Sonnet 5.5 用同一提示词做「切开的火山」，单个 HTML 文件，Three.js 负责画面，物理全部从零手写。作者列出四段：BUILD——用高度场抬起一座岛，火山锥按真实玄武岩层一层层堆起；CUT——把整块地形剖开，岩浆房、火山通道和熔岩管清楚可见；ERUPT——黏度和气体两个滑块决定是流出熔岩河还是爆炸喷出火山灰；GROW——熔岩入海冷却成新陆地，海岸线随之移动。作者给出的耗时与成本：Opus 5.5 1 小时 57 分、27.42 美元；Sonnet 5.5 2 小时 19 分、约 8.56 美元。封面可见两个版本的剖面地块：分层岩层、发光的岩浆房与右侧参数滑块。科普镜头：为什么有的火山「流」、有的火山「炸」（岩浆黏度与含气量）；夏威夷式熔岩造陆；「剖面 + 滑块」的交互形式也可迁移到刻蚀/沉积工艺剖面演示。

items.title: 整片日落大海只是一个 61 KB 的网页：WebGPU 从零手写 FFT 海浪、白浪和物理天空，Claude Code 约 30 分钟做出（MIT 开源）
items.description: GitHub 用户 Noniv 的开源项目（仓库 10月16日创建，MIT）；据 X 用户 @finebutwhy 转发时注明，原帖来自 Reddit r/ClaudeAI 用户 u/Any-Reputation8118，@jurlycat 转发称「据作者说用 Claude Code + Opus 5.5 约 30 分钟做出」。不用任何引擎或渲染库，直接在 WebGPU 上实时渲染日落海面：README 写明海浪是 Tessendorf FFT 模拟，6 级级联、每级 256×256，覆盖从约 1 公里到几毫米的波长；波谱为有限风区 JONSWAP 风浪 + Donelan-Banner 方向分布，再叠一层长峰涌浪；逆 FFT 用 compute shader 实现；海面网格是 17 级 CDLOD 四叉树，近处顶点间距 6.25 cm、远到 160 km。白浪从海面雅可比行列式「折叠」处生成并随风漂移、老化成条纹；天空按 Hillaire 大气散射方法，带两层云。未压缩的 ocean.html 102 KB，压缩版 61 KB，可直接 file:// 打开，WASD 自由飞行，H 键调风速、涌浪、太阳高度等参数。@jurlycat 转述作者说：Claude 用无头 Chrome 截图，再让子代理互相挑刺，作者主要只对云提了意见。科普镜头：海浪=很多正弦波叠加（傅里叶）、白浪出现在波面「折叠」处、为什么夕阳下海面会有一条闪光带。

items.title: 一段 1601 字中文提示词换来一片可玩的热带浅海：浪进浅水会变慢、贴着岸线转弯，Claude Code 先解程函方程再画水
items.description: X 用户 @Cryptoxorz 10月17日发布：把一段 1,601 字的中文提示词交给 Claude Code，得到一个 212 KB 的单文件网页——俯视的热带浅海（three.js r128，约 4,200 行）。可玩：点卡片把蝠鲼沿抛物线抛进海里溅起水花；拖着水母走会一路滴水；黑鳍礁鲨巡游时背鳍划出 V 形尾迹、碰一下会窜开；四个场景（热带浅滩、珊瑚潟湖、黄昏海湾、月夜荧光），夜里生物游过和浪打上沙滩处会亮起蓝绿荧光；还能下雨、开可拖动的漩涡。作者列出的做法：先算水深，再解程函方程（eikonal）得到浪到达每个点的时间，所以浪进浅水会变慢、贴着岸线转弯；海床预先烘焙成贴图并带接触阴影；阳光穿过水面形成焦散；水面是 GPU 上每秒推进 120 步的高度场，再叠长浪；最后合成折射、按水深吸收、泡沫与阳光碎闪。作者说第一版水是黑的、第二版一片白，是 Claude Code 自己开浏览器看效果、逐处修好的；宣传片画面也由网页逐帧渲染录制，配乐音效为代码合成。灵感来自 @vib3coded。科普镜头：浅水波速变慢导致的波浪折射（为什么海浪总是正对着海岸拍过来）。

items.title: 用 Claude 做视频的 5 步：参考→数据→故事→Remotion 代码动效→文字导演，不用视频模型
items.description: @francescoinweb3 2026-10-16 发帖：大多数 AI 视频看起来一样，是因为直接说「给我做个视频」。他每条视频都走同样 5 步，每步交给下一步一个真实文件：参考 spec.md（让 Claude 拆解喜欢的视频的节奏、第一个动作落点、剪辑节拍）→ 数据 data.json（先有真实数字，每个数字有出处）→ 故事 story.md（一个观点、一个主数字、三个节拍）→ 动效 Scene.tsx（用 Remotion 和 motion-design skill 把每一帧写成代码）→ 导演 timing.ts（用大白话给意见，如「标题晚了一拍」只改一行）；最后渲染静帧对照参考和数据检查，批准后才出 final.mp4。好处：没有视频模型所以不用重抽，同输入同结果，出问题知道是哪一步。引用其长文（完整设置、提示词和 10 个开源 skill）。

items.title: Opus 5.5 操控 Blender 搭出一间「有人住过」的书房：先给每件物体定物理规则，再决定哪些交给 Tripo 生成
items.description: X 用户 @shion_takk 10月16日发布：让 Claude Opus 5.5 通过 Blender MCP 操作 Blender，做一间虚构的书房（帖内两段视频+两张图）。作者总结：①需求定义最重要——定了公寓档次就能定房间骨架，定了结构类型就能定墙厚和窗框做法；②喂给 AI 一份「自己的经历」上下文文件，它会主动做出祖父做的能面、祖母烧的陶杯、网球拍等小物；③物体按三档生成：AI 用 bpy 直接建模 / Tripo HD / Tripo SM，按「需要怎么观察、之后要不要改形」来判定；④给所有物体套物理规则，逐件排查穿插和悬空；⑤反复强调「别自己发挥，先查专业资料」（例如窗框去看厂商目录）；⑥让显示器画面、小风扇等小东西动起来；⑦远景用生图代替。成本自述：98% 工作由 Opus 5.5（medium）完成，按 API 价折算约 455 美元（实际用 100 美元订阅），约 50 次提示、多为语音输入；Tripo 生成 41 次约 25 美元；回复中称历时 4 天，AI 工作约 18 小时，另渲染 13.5 小时。次日的制作复盘帖补充：给每件物体做干涉检查并按物理属性分类；搅拌机、网球拍先让 AI 调研构造再改；书脊文字方向也要修；做视频的话远景图应做成弧面。可作 Tripo + Blender 实际工作流参考。
items.tool: Claude Opus 5.5（medium，部分 Sonnet 5.5 子代理）+ Blender MCP + Tripo（HD/SM）+ GPT Images 2.5（经 Codex CLI 调用）（作者自述）

items.title: 中土世界做成一块漂浮的微缩沙盘：真实 GIS 地形 + Three.js WebGPU，逐帧录成 3 分 47 秒电影，代码全开源
items.description: X 用户 @Earthwalker17X 10月16日发布：用 Claude Code 里的 Opus 5.5 从零做出一个微缩 3D 中土世界，再把它拍成 3 分 47 秒的电影。仓库 README（MIT，代码）写明：1600×960 公里的中土地图放在一块漂浮的石板上，海岸线、河流、湖泊和起伏来自社区 ME-DEM 高程模型与 ME-GIS 矢量图层；Python 烘焙脚本把河流贴到谷底、求解湖面高度、推导地表覆盖；高度像立体地形模型一样被夸张；24 个地标（霍比屯、孤山、末日火山等）全部用代码建模；天空、水、烟和光都是实时渲染，没有预渲染；three.js r186 WebGPU + TSL，TypeScript strict；电影以 1080p24、227.75 秒逐帧确定性捕获，并配原创管弦乐。作者说难点仍是「普通的工程问题」：架构、一致性、视觉 QA、资源限制和迭代，并开源了代码、渲染管线、QA 工具和复现步骤。可作科普镜头参考：立体地图为什么要把山「拉高」、河流如何贴合谷底。

items.title: 开源一整支 Blender 3D 团队：概念设计到建模，Claude Code 通过 MCP 就能指挥
items.description: Scenario 联合创始人 Emmanuel de Maistre（@emmanuel_2m）2026-10-14 发帖：刚把「一整支 3D 团队」开源进 Blender。Scenario 插件可以在 Blender 里直接用，也可以交给 Claude Code，通过 MCP 指挥。帖子按文件夹列出岗位：概念设计师（一句话出概念图、从当前视口取参考）、3D 艺术家（文字或照片生成网格，给选中的网格重贴图或重拓扑）、动画师（给选中角色绑骨、用文字出动作）、材质师（任意材质槽上 PBR、用照片出贴图）、布局师（一段描述出灰盒、360 世界和天空）、摄影师（一句话出相机路径：环绕、推拉、升降、飞越）、渲染师（视口出静帧、预览出成片）、声音设计（音乐、人声、音效落到序列器）。公开仓库 scenario-labs/blender-plugin（GPL-3.0-or-later，Blender 5.0+）写明：在视口里生成图像、视频、3D 和 PBR 材质，并在本机提供 MCP。帖内为约 79 秒演示。可拍角度：①一个插件拆成八个岗位的流水线；②同一句需求，Claude Code 经 MCP 改视口里的网格；③从灰盒到成片，适合 3D 建模向口播。

items.prompt:
# Satellite Briefing — Style Prompt

> Real satellite imagery of a real place, graded down to an analyst's grey, with thin white measurement lines drawn on the ground: a lock-on reticle, outlines, a range line, one reading. One continuous zoom built from stacked imagery plates carries the viewer from orbit to the ground and back, and time can run inside one locked frame.
> References (grammar only): open-source investigation films that annotate satellite pictures (thin lines on imagery, one claim per screen, measuring as the plot); the Eameses' *Powers of Ten* (one continuous change of scale with a readout); NASA Earth Observatory's *World of Change* (one place, time running). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, icons or music; never name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The ground is a photograph**: real, licence-clean, georeferenced satellite or aerial imagery of the actual place. Nothing on the ground is drawn, stylised or generated.
- **Two layers, two truths**: the imagery is what the satellite saw; the hairlines are what the analyst measured. Marks are thin, white, sparse, and sit on real coordinates.
- **The grade moves with the story**: orbit in true colour, the analysis layer in grey, colour back only where the story turns.
- **Scale is the camera**: one zoom from orbit to the ground built from nested plates, with an altitude readout and a scale bar from the same camera.
- **One finding per screen**, in the single accent colour.

Not Data Storytelling (a chart on paper), not Sci-fi Hologram HUD (no glowing wireframes or invented chrome), not Blueprint, not Isometric Infographic (real nadir or oblique views, no diorama), not a keynote (no slides, header bars or chapter numbers).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Plates**: georeferenced rasters with a lon/lat box, sampled in a shader where the camera ray hits the ground, nested by resolution (world → region → detail) with feathered edges so finer plates dissolve in as the camera descends.
- **Globe**: ray–sphere from a perspective camera, a thin atmosphere rim, limb shading at orbit only; compute |C|² − R² in double precision (float32 fails below a few tens of km).
- **Time**: dated plates share one grid. A soft scan front (a satellite pass, never a hairline) swaps them: north → south forward, south → north for a rewind. Growth can run outward from the old edge, ordered by a distance map.
- **The analyst's grade** (one uniform from colour to grey): luminance with local contrast and clarity, a shoulder so salt, snow and cloud stay below white, toned blue-black → cool silver up to ~65 % grey, a fifth of the chroma. White belongs to the marks.
- **Marks**: a 2D overlay through the same world → screen function: hairlines 1.2–2.6 px with a dark halo, dashes for history and claims, brackets, ticks, leader lines. Lines draw on; outlines print behind the scan.
- **Screen space only for instruments** (altitude, scale bar, imagery credit) and the transcript strip. Everything else is anchored to the ground.
- **The claim layer** is a printed map drawn in the shader from a distance field of the old outline: paper grain a few pixels wide at any zoom, halftone ink, coast and waterlines, graticule, the serif name.
- **Post**: light grain in ffmpeg, a vignette, directional blur only on whip pans.

## 3. Colour logic

- Neutral ground: grey, roughly 3–65 % in value. White means *measured*.
- One accent (warm, e.g. amber) for the single reading on screen, never decoration.
- A second hue may mark the **claim** the imagery tests (a map, a plan, a promise): flat, cartographic, never used for anything measured.
- True colour is evidence: at orbit, and again only where the story turns (the field that greened, the water that returned).
- No false-colour ramps over the imagery.

Example (our demo): ground #070B0E → #A1A7A9, marks #F2F5F6, reading #FFBE55, map blue rgb(46, 112, 206).

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Roles**: a light condensed grotesk for the reading (96–130 px, e.g. Barlow Condensed); a monospace for instruments and dates (20–34 px, e.g. IBM Plex Mono); a sans for labels in the film's language (24–42 px); a serif only for the claim layer and the title. OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset to the characters used.
- **Labels attach to the ground** with a leader line. The reading sits in the right third beside what it measures, label above, source note below ("Landsat, measured").
- **Subtitles are a transcript strip** at the bottom left: a 2 px white rule, a dark plate fading right, left-aligned, each line on one line (measure with the real font, `nowrap`; split a long sentence into two cues). If the film is bilingual, the film's language on top.
- Nothing below 20 px at 1080p, the imagery credit included.
- Hold subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); a rolling counter reports its landing value; labels stay ≥ characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5 s (CJK).

## 5. Motion quality

- The camera never stops: distance interpolates in log space, segments ease, holds keep a 2–5 % creep or a slow rotation. No frozen frame longer than a second.
- Marks arrive by being made: a line grows, an outline prints behind the scan, a counter rolls and lands with a small pop, a reticle snaps with overshoot.
- Time changes are scans, never dissolves; their spacing tells the speed, and the camera moves with them (accelerating as the steps shorten, braking on the last).
- Never moves: the ground under its annotations, the instrument positions.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Oblique orbit, limb in frame | scale, context, distance | an opening; a return; a title card |
| Dive (log zoom, tilt to nadir) | going to look for yourself | a reveal; checking a claim |
| Locked nadir frame, slow creep | evidence, comparison | time running in one place; a measurement |
| Push-in on a point | singling out | one town, one dam, one field |
| Track along a line | travelling a distance | measuring; a river, a road, a border |
| Whip pan with blur | a new subject at the same altitude | the counter-example; "meanwhile" |
| Climb back to orbit | consequence, perspective | an ending; a summary |

At key moments the subject fills a third of the frame height; reading right, subtitles bottom left, instruments in the corners. Transitions: scan-line swaps, a map layer switched off, zooming through plates, whip pans, the reticle opening into a title card. No crossfades between unrelated places, no hard cuts inside a zoom.

## 7. Sound palette

- **Telemetry**: FM pings (a lock-on ping worth bringing back), dry ticks on the grid that divide to accelerate, noise scans (rising for a rewind, falling forward), servo whines, a ratchet for a range line.
- **Weight**: timpani, bass drum, gran cassa, bowed cymbal, a tam-tam reversed when time runs backwards. Measurements land on a pitched hit.
- **Synthesis**: a pulse bass with audible 2nd and 3rd harmonics, detuned-saw pads under a low-pass, risers for dives.
- **Beds**: orbit hum, radio hiss, data chatter; the place's own ambience (wind, water, a far horn), sparingly, often as J- or L-cuts.
- **One option for the shape**: keep the palette dry (electronics, skins, metal) and let one wet timbre (glass, water, bowed metal) mark the turn.
- **Silence**: music and foley stop, a thin bed stays, impacts may decay into it; the first sound after it is the turn. A short suck-out (0.2–0.45 s, music and foley down ~25 dB) before the heaviest impacts makes them land.
- **Mix**: voice ~10 dB over music; the two or three designed impacts are the loudest moments (out of the bus compressor, with mid-range body, e.g. a low-brass stab); 20–60 Hz about 15 dB under the full band (high-pass ~40 Hz, impact weight at 60–120 Hz); −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.2 dB. Voice: a calm analyst, short declarative lines.

## 8. Native moves

- **The map against the photograph.** The camera falls into the printed map of the claim; a scanner bar tears it away and the ground is underneath; the name outlives the page. *Fits content like:* a lake still on maps but gone; a cleared concession forest; a planned city never built.
- **Time rings in a locked frame.** Dated plates scan in one by one; each leaves its outline, the band lost between two rings flashes. *Fits content like:* a glacier's retreat; a city's sprawl; a fire scar season after season.
- **The range line.** Mark the destination, grow a ticked line from A to B, chase the tip while the reading counts up, land on the number, pull back to show the whole distance. *Fits content like:* how far a shore moved; a village to its well; a camp to the border.
- **The dive and the climb.** One zoom from orbit to the ground, or back. *Fits content like:* locating anything; a scale reveal; an ending that returns one place to the planet.
- **Colour returns where the story turns.** Only the subject regains true colour inside the grey. *Fits content like:* an irrigated field; a refilled reservoir; a regrown forest.
- **The reticle becomes the frame**: the lock-on brackets open out to frame a title card or the last reading.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Licences**: not usable: Google Earth/Maps, Bing, Esri World Imagery, Mapbox Satellite, Planet, Maxar, news photos, AI-generated imagery. EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless is CC BY 4.0 only for 2016 (2018 onward is NC). Raw Copernicus Sentinel data need "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [year]"; check the user's rules. Public domain or free with credit: USGS Landsat (1972 on, worldwide), USGS NAIP (US, ~1 m), NASA Blue Marble, MODIS, VIIRS. Burn a readable credit into the picture and list every asset in `CREDITS`.
- **Finding imagery for a new place**: search by bounding box and date in the Planetary Computer STAC (Landsat C2, Sentinel-2 L2A; no account) or USGS EarthExplorer; MODIS/VIIRS and Blue Marble from NASA GIBS; outlines from Natural Earth. Log every request. OSM (ODbL), CC BY-SA and "no known restrictions" are not CC0: name the terms and ask the user first. Ask for the user's own surveys or GIS layers when the place is theirs. Never fill a gap with generated imagery presented as evidence.
- **Seams**: paths imaged on other days disagree. One date per path, each scene gain-matched on stable land, feathered overlaps, holes filled from the same year only.
- **Old sensors**: Landsat MSS (to 1992) has no blue or SWIR and drops scan lines: nearest-neighbour resampling, near-zero rows as nodata filled from same-year scenes, scan-angle streaks cleaned on land only. Inspect every year at full contrast.
- **Plumes and haze** cross water as bright diagonal bands: swap the scene for another date of the same year rather than painting it out.
- **Edges**: resampling against nodata darkens scene rims (erode the mask); drop contour pieces along a plate border. Real straight edges (dikes, polders) can read as seams: frame them out or label them.
- **Grey mush at close range**: raise local contrast for that altitude only and dim outside the measured corridor.
- **Water and cloud**: MNDWI where shortwave infrared exists, only the basin you measure; clouds read as features in grey, so use the dry season.
- **Facts**: keep a FACTS.md in the project folder (claim, source URL, quoted wording, or the measurement method with scene IDs and dates) and deliver it with the film. Measure on the date you show.

## 10. Engine

- `demo/engine.js`: `makeCamera({lat, lon, d, tilt, heading, sx, sy})`, `project()` / `unproject()`, the WebGL2 plate shader (nested plates, time scans, growth map, analyst grade, printed-map layer, whip blur).
- `demo/overlay.js`: hairlines, brackets, `readout`, the measured single-line `subtitle` strip, `text` with a registry for `window.TEXTS`.
- `demo/tools/`: `fetch_landsat.py` (STAC, one date per path, same-year gap fill), `plates.py` (normalisation, streak cleaning, water masks, areas), `vectors.py` (shorelines, distances), `mapfield.py` (the printed map), `growth.py`.
- **Extra packages and packs**: none beyond `setup.sh deps voice` and the sample packs the score uses (`sh tools/fetch.sh instruments <lib>` for vsco2ce, vcsl, freepats in the demo). Imagery uses only the standard library, numpy, SciPy, Pillow (no GDAL); allow 3–4 GB for cached scenes. Anything more (rasterio, pyproj) goes in a private venv in the project folder, not `$LIB/.venv`.

## 11. Variation space

The agent decides the place or places, whether there is a claim layer, which dates, the structure, the camera path, the accent hue and where colour comes back.

- **Structures**: a locked time-lapse of one place ending in a push-in; a river followed from source to mouth with a reading at each stop; two places compared at one scale with whip pans.
- **Openings**: a ground-level detail that climbs to reveal its scale; a black frame a scan line paints in; an oblique orbit with a searching reticle.
- **Endings**: the climb back to orbit; a last measurement that lands and holds in silence; the claim layer redrawn to match the ground.

---

How our demo was made (story, shots, score, end card, build): [DEMO.md](DEMO.md). Read it after your treatment exists.

items.prompt:
# Engineering Briefing Board — Style Prompt

> One real whiteboard wall, filmed: window light on enamel, ghosts of erased marker, frame and tray. Cut-out photographs of real things land on it with weight; tags, magnets, a ruler and stamps are pinned to it; marker ink draws itself in three colours with fixed meanings. The camera rides the lines from fact to fact and only at the end pulls back to show the whole briefing.
> References (grammar only): explainers filmed on a map wall; the long pull-back over a wall covered in work; drafting conventions (plan above elevation, dimension lines, hatching). Never copy them or name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

1. **A physical board in a room**: enamel, window falloff, a sliding reflection, ghosts of earlier work, frame and tray.
2. **Real things on it**: cut-out photographs of the real objects, a few millimetres off the board, shadowed by one window, parallaxing. They are evidence: never a generated image presented as a real object.
3. **Ink that means something**: graphite for names and rules, blue for water and measurement, red only for the decision; rejected ideas erased to ghosts.
4. **One continuous wall**: no pages; the camera travels along lines, projections and leaders.
5. **The whole wall, once**: every shot is a crop of the final briefing, seen whole only in the last pull-back, as a poster.

Not **Whiteboard Explainer** (a hand drawing line art on a flat page): the board is a filmed object, subjects are photographs. Not **Data Storytelling**: comparisons are dimension lines in real units beside real objects. Not a keynote: no headers, centred bullets, page turns.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Board (z 0)**: procedural enamel, wiped ghost strokes, smudges, a window falloff, a sliding diagonal reflection; the frame shadows a warm grey wall.
- **Ink (multiply)**: flat colour at about 90 %, lighter core, round caps, a wet-tip glint on the stroke being drawn. Lettering: a marker font revealed glyph by glyph with seeded tilt and baseline jitter. Erasing leaves a blurred ghost (about 7 %).
- **Prints (z ≈ 6–14)**: photographs cut out at full resolution (a matting model, or a hand polygon / mask), clean edges, one shared grade (lower saturation, a touch warmer, lifted blacks). Thin structure (cables, wires, masts, railings) is measured in the photo and redrawn as clean lines in one colour. Shadow = blurred silhouette along one light vector, softer the higher the object. **No frame upsamples a photo**: ≥ 1 source px per screen px at its largest, measured; cap the zoom or find a bigger source.
- **Secondary layer** (only where the camera never goes before the end): the photos as pinned prints, a source card, sums on sticky notes, a small sketch. Texture and proof for the final wall, lighter than the main line.
- **Props (z ≈ 8–26)**: magnetic tags, magnets, a steel ruler, printed cards, a pitted stamp impression; the tray (z 70) nearest the lens.
- **Camera**: parallax by height, sub-frame motion blur (180° shutter), light grain. Only subtitles are screen-space.

## 3. Colour logic

- Ground: the enamel and its light falloff; the wall around is neutral warm grey.
- Ink: graphite = names, rules, facts; blue = water and measurement (dimensions, projection lines, measured numbers); red = the decision (a rejection, the key word of a verdict, the one mark to notice); grey for drafting only (extension lines, hatching).
- Red is rare: two or three red marks per frame at most, never on a red object. Full colour belongs to the photographs; props stay neutral; a red magnet is a verdict.

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Marker lettering**: a single-weight marker face covering every script the film uses (ours: LXGW Marker Gothic, OFL, subset — re-run when words change). Content 100–160 board px; a verdict 230–400.
- **Printed labels** (tags, cards, stamps): a sturdy sans; credit lines in a monospace. A tag holds one to three words.
- **Subtitles**: a frosted acrylic strip at the bottom centre with a blue marker tick. If the film is bilingual, the film's language sits on top. **One line per language**: `nowrap`, measured in the page against a 1,500 px safe width; a long line becomes two cues. Key content stays above the strip (bottom 15 %).
- **Reading time**: subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); board text stays fully in frame for CJK ÷ 4.5 + other ÷ 15 + 1.5 s from when it appears. In the final wall, text meant to be read is ≥ 20 px on screen.

## 5. Motion quality

- 24 fps on ones; nothing is stepped.
- Camera: overlapping eased moves, velocity ∝ u^a (1−u)^b (a, b ≈ 1.5–4), so speed and acceleration never jump; b > a gives inertia. A hand-held breath (≤ 3 px) underneath; shake only on an impact.
- Weight: prints are lowered from the camera side, land, bounce and settle as the shadow tightens; magnets clack on to pin them; tags swing; removed magnets pop toward the lens; struck things jolt and spring back. The camera may meet a landing close, briefly, on the object's most telling detail, then pulls out.
- Blurred in motion, sharp where words are read. Every 1–2 beats something lands, draws or swings; only silences and judgement holds go still.
- Ink draws at the speed of a hand; dimension lines land with an arrowhead tap.
- Never: dissolves, scale-pops on text, bouncy UI easing, text fading in by itself.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Ride a line (with the pen or a dimension) | measuring; "how far does it go?" | lengths compared; a route; a timeline |
| Tilt along projection lines | the same quantity in another view | plan → elevation; a total → its parts |
| Slow push-in, slight Dutch tilt | tension, an approaching problem | a collision; a deadline; an overrun |
| Pull back and sideways | stepping back to state a rule | a constraint; a turn in the argument |
| Whip with the line, overshoot, settle | a result that exceeds | a record; an outlier |
| Rise along a leader line | from evidence to verdict | a conclusion; a recommendation |
| Staircase framing (each new item with the previous result) | comparison in sequence | rankings; tests; options |
| Judgement frame: the whole item, the limit and the verdict, held ≥ 2.5 s | a test the viewer can check | pass / fail against a threshold; a budget against a cap |
| Long pull-back to the whole wall | scale; everything at once | the end of an argument; a summary |

Framing: off-centre, cropped, close. The first frame holds a readable subject; the first strong action hits within 0.5 s. Items tested against a limit each get a judgement frame (wider each time if they grow); the verdict lands after the camera settles. Before the reveal: ≤ about 60 % of the board's width, never both side edges, never the reveal's zone. Transitions are moves; no cuts, fades or zoom-to-fit.

## 7. Sound palette

- Room: an air-conditioning bed and traffic through the window, about 20 dB under the voice — audible, not a hiss; silences keep only this.
- Foley: felt-tip squeaks scaled to stroke length, nib taps, magnet clacks (a pitch per magnet in a row), suction pops, print landings (board thump, paper slap), a ruler's ring, eraser felt, a stamp's thud.
- The subject's own sound arrives early as a J-cut; the first sound after a silence is an impact or the subject's sound.
- Music: a small rhythmic ensemble, walking to brisk — bass, a light kit, wooden percussion, low brass stabs for verdicts (or mallets); no piano-and-strings pad. Landings, stamps and arrows sit on the beat. Voice calm, briefing-room confident, about 8–10 dB over the music; −14 LUFS.

## 8. Native moves

- **The whole-wall reveal.** Design the wall as a poster first (hierarchy, reading path, filling the frame), then plan every shot as a crop of it; keep one zone (secondary layer, verdict, title card) for the reveal alone. *Fits:* a product roadmap; a household budget.
- **The subject passes through the answer.** The real thing moves through the chosen solution, its sound first. *Fits:* a parcel along the chosen route; a train over the new viaduct.
- **Ride the dimension line.** A quantity drawn as a real length to one scale; the camera rides the tip. *Fits:* battery ranges of four cars.
- **Projection lines.** Dashed lines carry an edge from one view to another so two drawings share a scale. *Fits:* a trail map above its elevation profile.
- **Magnets as countable things.** Units clack on in rhythm, pop off when a rule removes them. *Fits:* seats in a vote.
- **Erase to a ghost.** A rejected idea wiped but faintly visible. *Fits:* last year's plan under this year's.
- **The stamp.** A verdict lands with a thud and a jolt. *Fits:* passed / failed tests.
- **The physical answer.** A real prop laid down as the solution. *Fits:* one cable instead of five.
- **Leader to the verdict.** An arrow from the deciding number to the conclusion. *Fits:* the bottleneck in a process.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Text glimpsed in passing** fails the reading time. Fix: words where the camera rests; frame each new item with the last result.
- **Only close-ups.** The viewer never sees the whole object against the limit. Fix: detail → judgement frame → hold → verdict → move on.
- **Photos that don't belong together.** Fix: one grade, one light vector, one viewpoint family.
- **Thin parts lost or stair-stepped** by the matte. Fix: key them against the clean background, redraw clean lines at the measured positions.
- **Upsampled photos** go soft in close-ups. Fix: full-resolution cuts, large sources, a per-frame check.
- **Lettering in photos** (signs, names, logos). Fix: paint out, cut, or choose another photo.
- **The wall seen too early** spends the ending; **a sparse or tiny final wall** wastes it. Fix: measure every frame's visible share; size the hierarchy for the poster; a quiet secondary layer, no empty middle.

## 10. Sources, facts, engine

- **Photos**: Wikimedia Commons (read each file page's licence and author), national libraries and archives (e.g. the Library of Congress: check each item's rights statement), agency media pages, Flickr Commons. Fine: CC0, public domain, CC BY (credit it). CC BY-SA, "no known restrictions" (≠ CC0) or other terms: name them to the user and ask first. For the user's own product, site or people, ask for their photos. No licensable photo of a real thing → draw it in marker as a sketch; never a generated image presented as the real object.
- **Facts**: keep a `FACTS.md` in the project folder (each claim on screen or in the voice, its source URL, the quoted wording, or the measurement method) and deliver it with the film. List every photo in `CREDITS` with source, author and licence.
- **Extra packages and packs** (beyond `setup.sh deps voice music`): `onnxruntime` and the BiRefNet-general matting model (MIT, ~970 MB: https://github.com/danielgatis/rembg/releases/download/v0.0.0/BiRefNet-general-epoch_244.onnx, path in `$BIREFNET_ONNX`) for cut-outs; `fonttools` only to subset CJK fonts offline. The agent installs them itself into a private venv in the project folder (`demo/kit/tools/kit_env.sh` does venv and model), never into `$LIB/.venv`. Without the model: cut with `prep_object.py --poly` (hand polygon) or `--mask` (a mask image).
- **Engine** (copy into the project): `demo/kit/board.js` (camera, prints, tags, magnets, ruler, cards, stamp, ink, erasing, `sceneTexts(t)`, `subCheck()`; fields in `demo/kit/README.md`), `demo/kit/batch.mjs` (stills), `demo/kit/tools/` (cut-outs, line redraws, lettering wipe, prints, fonts), checks in `demo/tools/` (`camcheck.mjs` visible share and judgement frames, `rescheck.mjs`, `subcheck.mjs`).

A minimal world (`node demo/kit/batch.mjs park.json`; `fetch_fonts.py park.json` first for new characters):

```json
{ "dur": 6, "t": 5.5, "board": { "w": 4000, "h": 2400 }, "hand": 0, "cam": { "x": 1500, "y": 1000, "z": 0.8, "moves": [] },
  "elements": [
    { "type": "tag", "text": "地下车库", "xy": [560, 800], "size": 60, "arrive": { "t": 0.2, "kind": "swing" } },
    { "type": "ink", "kind": "dim", "from": [700, 900], "to": [1300, 900], "color": "blue", "t": 0.6, "d": 0.6 },
    { "type": "ink", "kind": "write", "text": "120 米", "xy": [1360, 940], "size": 100, "color": "blue", "t": 1.2 },
    { "type": "stamp", "text": "首选", "xy": [1500, 700], "size": 110, "rot": -8, "t": 4.2 } ] }
```

## 11. Variation space

The agent decides per film: structure, which objects are photographed, plan vs elevation, the wall's reading path, opening, ending, camera path, pacing.

- **Three structures:** one measurement that keeps growing until it breaks a limit; a before/after where the erased first plan stays as a ghost under the second; a checklist stamped item by item as the camera moves down the wall.
- **Three openings:** a stamp on a finished drawing, then back to see why; one number written large, then the line that measures it; a photo dropped onto an empty corner.
- **Three endings:** the wall revealed with the answer circled; back to the opening mark, now corrected; the last tag flipped from a question to an answer, then the pull-back.

---

items.prompt:
# LiDAR Survey — Style Prompt

> Real airborne laser points of a real place, floating in the dark as a measured cloud; a scan line or a cutting plane passes through them and the points condense into a solid, raking-lit surface, which is then measured with hairline instruments. One designed camera move carries the whole film: the cloud is something you fly through, not a picture you look at.
> References (grammar only): survey and archaeology lidar visualisations (colour as height, the canopy removed); architectural section drawings (a cut, dimensioned); museum film cadence (one held reading per screen). Copy none of their layouts, ramps, typefaces or music, and never name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The cloud is the data**: every point is a real return at its measured position; points appear, glow, lift away or give way to a surface, but are never moved into a shape.
- **Points become a surface**: a front (scan line, cutting plane) behind which the cloud condenses into a solid model of the same place.
- **Classification is a lever**: ground, vegetation, buildings, water are layers to peel, isolate and recolour.
- **Measurement in hairlines**: one reading at a time, in the accent, attached to what it measures; numbers from the points or an official source.
- **Dark, quiet, exact**: near-black ground, restrained colour, no glow except at the front.

Not Sci-fi Hologram HUD (no invented interface: the points are real, sparse where the survey was), not Satellite Briefing (photographs from above; here a 3D cloud flown through), not Blueprint, not Low-poly Isometric, not Glass Product Render.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Points**: GL points sized in world units (0.12–0.3 m), floor of one output pixel, soft discs, opaque and depth-tested (additive only for a ghost layer); colour from height or class, value from intensity; distance fog.
- **Quantise for the browser**: uint16 positions (2 cm / 1 cm) plus a byte each for height above ground, class, intensity, seed.
- **Height above ground** for every return (minus a ground model triangulated from class-2 returns) drives the colour ramp, the cutting plane and the ruler.
- **The solid surface**: a 0.5–1 m mesh of the ground or surface model, smooth normals, baked short-radius AO, a low raking sun (20–35°), faint contours, crests lightened. Display exaggeration of micro relief (×2–3) only with an on-screen note; measure on undistorted data.
- **The front**: one world-space plane (one uniform) shared by the point and surface shaders; points ahead of it brighten, a thin seam glows behind it and the surface fills in over tens of metres.
- **The cutting plane** (by height above ground): returns above it lift away and fade, a ring glows where it meets the trees, a ruler on the frame edge tracks it.
- **Marks on the surface** (traced features, section lines) are a distance field in the surface shader, kept hairline with `fwidth`; readings, leaders and charts are a 2D overlay through the same world → screen function.
- **A survey window**: outside the measured area the cloud stays as dim points instead of ending in black.
- **Post**: 2× render, high-threshold bloom (only fronts and seams), vignette; no grain (points are already fine detail; encode at a higher CRF).

## 3. Colour logic

- Background near-black with a cold tint; never pure black, never a gradient sky.
- Points: one ramp by height or class, desaturated (deep green-teal → pale; or grey → white); intensity modulates value, not hue. No rainbow elevation ramps.
- The front and seams: one cool near-white; it is light, not a colour.
- The solid surface: warm neutral (stone, clay, plaster), lit; its colour never competes with the accent.
- One accent (amber) reserved for what was found and measured: traced features, the reading, the section line. A second, cooler hue only in a comparison chart.

Example (our demo): background #05080A, canopy #1F3F35 → #5C9A7A → #E2F3DC, ground returns #C8B38C, surface #BDB5A6, front #D4FFF0, accent #FFB347, chart green #83C495.

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Roles**: light condensed numerals for readings (110–130 px, e.g. Barlow Condensed 300); a monospace for instruments, coordinates, counts and source lines (19–22 px, e.g. IBM Plex Mono); a sans for labels in the film's language (24–36 px, e.g. Noto Sans SC 500). OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset to the characters used.
- **Instruments** in one corner: place, coordinates, area, data source, point count, any exaggeration; they change only when the medium does.
- **Readings** in the right third beside what they measure: label, number, source/method line; a leader when the feature is in frame; a rolling counter reports its landing value.
- **Subtitles**: a transcript strip bottom-left (2 px rule, plate fading right), one line per language measured with the real font, split rather than wrapped; if bilingual, the film's language on top.
- Nothing below 19 px at 1080p. Hold subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); labels ≥ characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5 s (CJK), letters ÷ 15 + 1.5 s (Latin).

## 5. Motion quality

- On ones, 24 fps; the camera never stops; keys as a C1 spline in target / distance / heading / pitch (no `lookAt` from nadir).
- The front moves on an ease, slowest where the subject is; a cutting plane steps on the beat (eased steps, short holds) so the layers read.
- Points appear behind a front or by height, never by random fade-in across the whole frame.
- Readings land with a small pop; traced features light up along their length in order.
- Never moves: the points relative to each other (no wobble, no noise displacement), the instruments' positions.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Locked nadir with slow push | "this is what a photo shows" | a claim to test; a before; an ending that returns to the map |
| Crane down with tilt to oblique | entering the data; the place has height | the switch from picture to cloud |
| Low oblique close to the cloud (10–20° pitch, 90–150 m) | volume; things standing up | canopy, buildings, a facade, a cliff |
| Slow orbit | studying, the plane doing the work | a peel; a scan; a held reading |
| Rising pull-back | scale reveal of what was found | a network, a site plan, a corridor |
| Lateral track | travelling a feature | a wall, a road, a pipeline, a coast |
| Push to a section | the detail that proves it | a cross-section, a clearance, a height |

Subject ≥ a third of the frame height at key moments; readings right third; instruments in a corner; nothing in the subtitle strip. Transitions are fronts and planes, never crossfades or hard cuts inside the cloud.

## 7. Sound palette

- **Instrument sounds**: FM pings, fine crackle as points arrive, noise sweeps tied to a front, ticks that divide (8ths → 16ths → 32nds) to accelerate, a descending pitched blip per peeled layer, a ratchet while a counter rolls, a ping when a reading lands.
- **Weight and synthesis**: timpani, bass drum, gran cassa for condensations and cuts, a reversed swell into the main impact; low-passed detuned-saw pads; a pulse bass with audible 2nd/3rd harmonics.
- **Dry and wet**: one option is electronics while the subject is still points, and a single organic, wooden or bowed timbre (marimba, bowed vibraphone) for the found features once the surface exists.
- **Beds**: the place's own ambience (wind in leaves, water, traffic) at the start and the end as J- and L-cuts; a thin air bed in between.
- **Silence**: a near silence (air only) before the main reveal; the first sound after it is the impact.
- **Mix**: voice ~10 dB over the music and ducking it; impacts outside the bus compressor; −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.2 dBTP. Voice: a calm, plain narrator, short declarative lines.

## 8. Native moves

- **Photo to points.** A scan line crosses an aerial photo; behind it the place is points. *Fits content like:* a site visit before a design; what the satellite misses; a quarry's real volume.
- **The canopy peel.** A plane descends by height above ground, returns above it lift away layer by layer, a ruler tracks it. *Fits content like:* archaeology under forest; a hidden trail; flood channels; landslide scars.
- **Points condense.** A front turns the remaining points into a solid surface; found features light up in order. *Fits content like:* a building scan to a BIM shell; a cliff to a hazard model; a street to a vehicle clearance model.
- **The section.** A plane crosses one feature; the profile glows and a dimensioned chart of the real returns hangs beside it. *Fits content like:* a levee's height; a bridge's clearance; a road cut.
- **The window.** The measured area is a stage inside the unmeasured cloud. *Fits content like:* a parcel; a corridor; a site boundary.
- **The regrowth.** The removed layer returns as a ghost over what was found. *Fits content like:* an ending; a clearing before/after; a buried pipe under a street.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Finding data for a new place**: USGS 3DEP (US) as Entwine Point Tiles per project at `https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/<project>/ept.json`, projects and footprints in `boundaries/resources.geojson` of github.com/hobuinc/usgs-lidar; bare-earth scouting through the 3DEP elevation ImageServer. OpenTopography (catalogue of many collections, licence per dataset). AHN (Netherlands, CC0). National portals, e.g. England's Environment Agency LiDAR (OGL), France IGN LiDAR HD (Licence Ouverte), Spain PNOA-LiDAR (CC BY 4.0), Finland NLS (CC BY 4.0), New Zealand LINZ (CC BY 4.0); read each portal's terms. Fetch a subset by box and depth, not whole tiles.
- **Licences**: public domain, CC0, CC BY and attribution-only government licences are fine, with credit in `CREDITS`. ODbL, CC BY-SA, "no known restrictions" (not CC0) or non-commercial terms: name them to the user and ask first. Never commercial scans or Google 3D tiles. Ask the user for their own scans (a site survey, a drone or terrestrial scan, their BIM) when the film is about their asset. Never stand in a generated or invented cloud for real evidence.
- **Facts**: keep a FACTS.md in the project folder (claim, source URL, quoted wording, or the measurement method) and deliver it with the film.
- **Coordinates**: EPT copies are often Web Mercator: convert to a local east/north/up frame first; check the vertical datum against known ground.
- **Leaf-off vs leaf-on**: leaf-off lidar reaches the ground but its canopy is sparse; say which season each layer is.
- **Classification is the provider's**: class 1 mixes vegetation, buildings and noise; drop 7 and 18; finish a cut below 0 m or low vegetation stays as stripes.
- **A dense cloud reads as a flat carpet** from afar: go close and low for volume; let the distance fog out.
- **Scan striping** is real texture; don't frame a reveal on it at grazing angles.
- **Traced features are interpretation**: say "traced", keep the tracing in a data file, snap it to the data, leave faint candidates out.
- **Privacy**: crop out houses and yards; keep the survey window on public or uninhabited land.

## 10. Engine

- `demo/film.js`: point shader (front, cutting plane, lift, ghost, window), surface shader (light, AO, contours, feature field, section), photo shader, camera spline (`camAt`), overlay (`reading`, `drawSection`, `subtitles`, readcheck registry).
- `demo/tools/`: `fetch_ept.py` (EPT subset), `terrain.py` (local frame, DTM), `walls.py` (relief model), `trace.py` (snap a tracing, measure), `profile.py` (section from raw returns), `build_data.py` (binaries + facts).
- **Extra packages and packs** (beyond `setup.sh deps voice music`): Python `laspy`, `lazrs` (LAZ decoding), `scikit-image` (relief and ridge tools), `fonttools` + `brotli` (CJK subset). They are not in the library's `.venv`: the agent installs them itself into a private venv in the project folder (the demo uses `demo/assets/raw/.venv`), never into `$LIB/.venv`. Fonts come from github.com/google/fonts (ofl/), fetched by script.
- Minimal example, not in the demo: a building scan. Points coloured by class, a vertical front sweeping the street; behind it a 1 m surface model; one reading (roof height above the street).

## 11. Variation space

The agent decides the place and dataset, which classes to peel or keep, the fronts and their directions, the camera route, the readings, the accent within the colour logic, and whether a photo or a map opens the film.

- **Structures**: a corridor flown end to end with three readings; two surveys of one place (erosion, construction) swapped by a front; one object scanned, cut and dimensioned.
- **Openings**: a black frame the scan paints in line by line; a street-level photograph that dissolves into its own returns; a top-down map that tilts up into the cloud.
- **Endings**: the cloud pulls back to show the whole survey tile; the removed layer returns as a ghost; the last reading holds while the points fade to the instruments.

---

items.prompt:
# Projection on White Model — Style Prompt

> A pure white massing model of a real place stands on a plinth in a dark room, and a projector paints data onto it as light: one layer at a time, falling on the surfaces that face it, spilling a little past the plate. The model never changes; only the light on it does.
> References (grammar only): projection-mapped planning models in city galleries (the dark room, the soft throw, colour only on white surfaces); macro model photography (shallow focus at rooftop height); editorial data graphics (one figure, one label, one source per layer). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, colours or music, and never name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The model is real geometry of a real place**: building footprints and heights from open data (§2), extruded at a stated scale (1:1000, 1:2000…). Nothing on the model is invented or "representative", and no generated image ever stands in for the place.
- **The model is white; data is light.** Colour is never painted into the material: it is projected, so it brightens surfaces that face the projector, fades on walls turned away, stops at the edge of the throw and reaches a little onto the plinth.
- **Layers arrive one at a time**, each with its own gesture of light (a wash, a pop-on, a rising level, a moving sun), and each answers the question the last one raised.
- **A physical room**: house lights, a projector that strikes and switches, a plinth, darkness around it. Lights out is where the data starts; lights up is where it ends.
- **Every number on screen is computed from the same buildings** that are on the table.

Not Isometric Infographic (no diorama or icons), not Low-poly Island (no invented terrain), not Sci-fi Hologram HUD (no wireframes; light lands on matter), not Satellite Briefing (no imagery), not a laser-scan or point-cloud film (no scan lines; light is projected, not measured).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Model**: matte white (≈ #F3F3F1, roughness ≈ 0.9), crisp edges; water a darker satin inlay in the base plate; bridges low white slabs; a thin base plate on a dark satin plinth.
- **Light model**: house light = one soft key + a neutral studio environment + AO on close shots. Projection = a term added to the lit surface in the shader: `colour × (0.42 + 0.58 · max(N·toProjector, 0)) × throw mask`, scaled by albedo, reduced on water. Never a texture on the mesh.
- **Building data is the material.** First look for the place's own open 3D or footprint-with-height data: 3DBAG (Netherlands, CC BY 4.0), PLATEAU (Japan, CC BY 4.0-compatible), city open-data portals (footprints with heights or floors, zoning, plans). Fine: CC0, public domain, CC BY (credited in CREDITS and on screen). OpenStreetMap and Overture (ODbL), CC BY-SA and "no known restrictions" are not CC0: name the terms to the user and ask first. For their own site, ask the user for their data (plan, city model, survey heights).
- **Layers depend on what exists.** Construction years per building are a Dutch luxury (BAG); elsewhere they are often missing. Substitute what the data does hold and the medium can still project: heights or floor counts, footprint area, zoning or plan status, a boundary, sun and shadow (always computable). Never invent a year layer.
- **A layer is state, not a picture**: per-building attributes (year, height, rank, flags) live in vertex data; the shader decides each frame what colour the projector gives them.
- **The sun is a real directional light** with shadow maps, computed from the place's latitude and a real date and time (NOAA/Meeus solar position). The projector can trace what the sun does (a shadow footprint) but never fakes a shadow.
- **Post**: physical depth of field (stronger on close shots), bloom only above the projection highlights, vignette, light grain in ffmpeg. GTAO only on close shots: on wide grazing views it bands.
- **Screen space only for the 2D layer**: readouts, pins, measured lines and subtitles go through the camera's world → screen function so they stay pinned to the model.
- **Keep a FACTS.md in the project folder** (claim, source URL, quoted wording, or the measurement method) and deliver it with the film; every number on screen is computed by a script from the same data as the model.

## 3. Colour logic

- Neutral ground: white model, dark room (near black), dark plinth. Projector black level is a cool near-black on the plate.
- **One hue family per layer**, chosen for the data: a single categorical accent for "the old/the exception" (e.g. warm amber), a sequential ramp for continuous data (blue → cyan → white for time, violet → magenta → peach for height).
- **A colour may return** only with the same meaning (the "before" colour reused later marks the same set of buildings).
- The sun is warm, its shade is a projected deep blue; data colours are put away when the sun arrives.
- Never colour the model in the house light; never use more than two layer palettes on screen at once.

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Roles**: a light grotesk for the figure (Inter Tight 200, 120–140 px), a sans for labels in the film's language (Noto Sans SC 300/500, 20–36 px), a monospace for instruments, years and coordinates (IBM Plex Mono, 18–22 px). OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset.
- **Readout in the left third**, one per layer: index + layer name, one figure, one label, one source line, a legend bar.
- **Pins**: a hairline from a roof or a ground point up to a tag on a dark plate (title 26 px + one sub line 20 px).
- **Identity label** top-left, quiet: place, scale, data sources.
- **Subtitles** centred at the bottom on a soft dark gradient, no box, measured with the real fonts; if the film is bilingual, the film's language on top, each language on a single line, split into two cues rather than wrap.
- Nothing below 18 px at 1080p. Hold subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); labels ≥ characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5 s (CJK), letters ÷ 15 + 1.5 s (Latin).

## 5. Motion quality

- The camera moves continuously and slowly; it changes speed with the layers, never stops dead.
- **Light is the actor.** Each layer arrives by a soft-edged gesture of light: a wash spreading from the projector axis, buildings switching on one by one with a short flash, a level climbing every facade, the sun's clock running. No hard line sweeping the table.
- House lights cut fast (a relay, 0.25 s) and return slowly (1 s); the projector strikes with a brief flicker.
- Counters roll while the light moves and land when it lands; measured lines grow from A to B with ticks.
- What never moves: the model, the plinth, the pins' anchors on the model.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Macro glide at rooftop height, shallow focus | the model is a real object | an opening; a detail that matters |
| Crane up and back | the whole pattern only seen from above | revealing a hole, a cluster, an edge |
| Slow orbit with a rise | the city as a whole, layers accumulating | growth over time; comparisons across the model |
| Boom down to a low angle against black | height, skyline | tall buildings, heights, a single tower |
| Side-on track along a line | a measured distance on the model | a shadow, a corridor, a route, a view line |
| Pull back as the house lights return | the data stops; the object remains | an ending; a reset between topics |

At key moments the subject fills a third of the frame height; readouts left third, subtitles bottom centre, pins never over the readout. Transitions are light changes on one take (lights out, a layer replacing another, the projector going dark), not cuts, fades or wipes.

## 7. Sound palette

- **The room**: room tone, the projector fan (hum + filtered air) rising when the lamp strikes, relays for the house lights, a lamp strike (zap + thump), the air of a light wash (sliding band-passed noise).
- **Light as sound**: mallets and glass for things switching on, bowed vibraphone for held light, a rising mallet line and air riser for a climbing level, one glass note per highlighted building.
- **Weight**: timpani, gran cassa, gong, low brass for a heavy fact; warm low brass for a turn.
- **Floor**: contrabass and cellos only as a floor under the chords; no generic piano and strings melody.
- **Silence**: the projector goes dark and everything stops but a thin fan hum before the turn; a short suck-out before the heaviest hit. The first sound after the silence is the turn.
- **Mix**: voice about 10 dB over the music; the two designed impacts are the loudest moments; −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.2 dB. Voice: calm, short declarative lines, numbers spoken plainly.

## 8. Native moves

- **Lights out, lamp on.** House light, a relay, darkness, the lamp strikes, the first layer arrives. *Fits content like:* a site before and after; a district before a plan is shown; any "now look closer".
- **The hole.** Light only the set that answers a question (built before a date, owned by one party, inside a zone) and let the absence draw the shape. *Fits content like:* a war-damaged centre; a flood plain with no housing; land a company owns; a protected zone.
- **Layers by time.** Buildings switch on in the decade they were built, each layer faster than the last, a year counter rolling. *Fits content like:* a new town's growth; a campus master plan by phase; a port's expansion; a developer's portfolio by year.
- **The rising level.** A soft level of light climbs every facade at once; low buildings finish first, the tallest last, the reading rides up with it. *Fits content like:* building heights; sea-level or flood depth; floor counts; a height limit being tested.
- **The sun clock.** A real sun at a real date sweeps the shadows; the projector then traces one shadow and measures it. *Fits content like:* a new tower's shadow on a park; winter light in a courtyard; solar panels' best roofs; a street's daylight hours.
- **The pick-out.** One building or set lights alone while the rest stay dark, with a pin. *Fits content like:* a listed building; the plot for sale; the hospital in an evacuation plan.
- **Lights up.** The data stops, the white model comes back. An ending or a reset.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Wall normals** wound the wrong way show inside faces (walls look hollow): derive the outward normal from ring orientation. **Shared walls** between parts z-fight: skip the overlap below the lower neighbour.
- **Warm HDRIs turn the white model beige**: use a neutral studio environment.
- **GTAO on wide grazing views** produces wedge-shaped dark bands; keep it on close shots only.
- **A low sun lights facades, not roofs**: shoot from the sunlit side or side-on. **Narrow shadows vanish** among all the others: trace the one that matters (fill + edge) and measure it.
- **Hairline scan lines read as laser scanning**: give every projection front a wide soft edge or switch buildings individually.
- **Floating labels**: anchor pins on the tallest part of a building, not on its footprint centroid.
- **Numbers from mixed sources** (official height vs measured roof): say which on screen ("roof", "measured").

## 10. Engine

- `demo/studio.js` — `makeStudio(W, H, model)`: renderer, post, room, the projection material (`projMaterial(kind)` injects `projLight()` / `roofGlow()` into MeshStandardMaterial), the city mesh (`buildCity`: outward normals, shared walls removed), plate, plinth, house light (index 0) and sun (index 1). Uniforms `U` drive every layer.
- `demo/tools/prep.py` — **3DBAG + BGT only**: it reads 3DBAG fields (`b3_h_70p`, `b3_h_maaiveld`, `oorspronkelijkbouwjaar`) and Dutch RD coordinates (`tools/rd.py`). Another source needs its own adapter that writes the same `model.json`: `{size:[w,d] model metres, b:[[year|0, height_m], …] per building, p:[[building_index, height_model_m, [[[x,z],…] outer ring, …holes]], …] per roof part, decks:[[[x,z],…]]}`, with x east, z south, 1 unit = 1 model metre; plus `water.png` (plate-sized mask) and a `stats.json` with every on-screen number. `tools/sun.py` (solar position, any place and date) and the heightfield shadow are source-independent.
- `demo/overlay.js` — readout, pin, measured range line, subtitle strip, title card; registers texts for readcheck.
- **Extra packages and packs**: none beyond `setup.sh deps` (+ `voice`, `music` for narration and score); downloads are plain `curl` from the data portal. Reprojecting another country's data may need pyproj or shapely: the agent installs them itself into a private venv in the project folder, not into `$LIB/.venv`.
- Minimal example, not in the demo: set `U.uPreC` to a station and `U.uPreR` growing to light everything within walking distance; or put a flood height in `U.uHgtF` with `U.uHgtBand` held at 1 and leave it still.

## 11. Variation space

Decide per film: place and scale, which layers in what order, their colours, the opening, the camera path, the ending, the pace.

- **Structures**: a question answered layer by layer; a plan versus today (the plan's buildings switching on in a second colour); one building's story told by its neighbours.
- **Openings**: a macro glide over white roofs; darkness and a single pick-out; the plinth from across the room as the house lights fall.
- **Endings**: lights up on the white model; one last layer left on alone; the camera rising until the model is an object on a table in a dark room.

---

How our demo was made (story, shots, score, title card, build): [DEMO.md](DEMO.md). Read it after your treatment exists.
